key_insight: Automated Marker Expression Level (MEL) scoring quantified lung adenocarcinoma biomarkers and supported prognostic stratification comparable to expert visual scoring.
clinical_relevance: This framework could support scalable prognostic biomarker assessment, but it evaluates prognosis rather than drug discovery or treatment selection.
method: Segment tissue regions using a machine-learning Fiji plugin.
Calculate tumour-area-weighted MEL scores for BRCA1, GLUT1 and QKI, normalizing staining variability.
Combine MEL scores with tumour stage in a Cox-derived Combined Prognostic Index.
evidence_signal: In 128 patients, MEL correlated with visual H-scores (Spearman ρ = 0.61–0.69; p < 0.001), and the combined index separated disease-free and overall survival risk groups (p < 0.05).
watch_item: Independent external validation is not described in the abstract, and segmentation performed less well in highly immune-infiltrated stroma.
paper_title: Development and Validation of an Automated Image-Based Method for Prognostic Stratification in Lung Adenocarcinoma using Immunohistochemical Markers
